nodes.question: Why did the technology using MFCs not gain much traction despite initial interest?
nodes.answer: Subsequent proposals for using MFCs lacked clear, targeted objectives, which hindered further development.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Carbon capture and storage|Technological innovation in ccs_qna_001
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: What type of drug delivery system was developed to improve the application of Cel?
nodes.answer: An injectable water-in-oil emulsion hydrogel (EHG) was developed to improve the application of Cel.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Carbon capture and storage|Technological innovation in ccs_qna_002
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: What was the main focus of the research presented in the paragraph?
nodes.answer: The main focus of the research was to demonstrate the therapeutic efficacy of Gel@Cel-induced immunogenic cell death (ICD) and immune activation for the management of malignant ascites.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Carbon capture and storage|Technological innovation in ccs_qna_003
nodes.label: Strategy
nodes.question: What does Climeworks aim to do with its technology in the United States?
nodes.answer: Climeworks aims to upscale its technology in the United States through projects such as Project Cypress in Louisiana, Prairie Com-pass DAC Hub in North Dakota, and California DAC Hub in California.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Carbon capture and storage|Technological innovation in ccs_qna_004
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: What technological advancements have contributed to the increased availability of micro-XCT?
nodes.answer: Advancements include scintillator-coated microscopes and improvements in X-ray sources that reduce the X-ray spot size, enhancing the spatial resolution of the system.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Carbon capture and storage|Technological innovation in ccs_qna_005
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: What are some specific applications of laboratory-based micro-XCT mentioned in the paragraph?
nodes.answer: Applications include quantifying voids and cracks, examining internal interfaces, measuring surface roughness, and identifying post-test sample changes across various scales.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Carbon capture and storage|Technological innovation in ccs_qna_006
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: How does integrating XCT with other examination techniques benefit material analysis?
nodes.answer: It enables correlative microscopy, allowing for information gathering on a sample from the engineering length scale down to the atomic level.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Carbon capture and storage|Technological innovation in ccs_qna_007
nodes.label: Management
nodes.question: What is crucial for accelerating the development of ultra-low-carbon technologies?
nodes.answer: Accelerating the development of ultra-low-carbon technologies requires a societal and economic transformation alongside scientific advancements, as well as identifying key factors that drive innovation.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Carbon capture and storage|Technological innovation in ccs_qna_008
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: What is the primary focus of the research article regarding the Fe-Si system?
nodes.answer: The research article focuses on a hybrid update of the Fe-Si system by experimentally examining phase equilibria and thermodynamic properties using Differential Scanning Calorimetry (DSC) and High-Temperature Laser Scanning Confocal Microscopy (HT-LSCM) to improve heat management and process control in producing silicon steels.
